natural_body: Targeted 40% discounts boost acquisition but sharply damage retention.

first.rationale: The two acute symptoms are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), so the highest-leverage direction is the one that acts directly on the funnel stage that regressed. memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifts completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer required signup fields lifts first-week SMB activation) both point at simplify_onboarding, and they are mutually reinforcing rather than a single data point — which is exactly why I want the archived records: consolidated one-line summaries have lost effect size, sample, segment, and the conditions under which the lift held. I need to know whether memory_31's lift was measured on the same SMB self-serve population now being poached, whether memory_86's 'durable' claim was measured past week one, and whether either was run against a competitive-pricing backdrop. If the source records show thin or narrow evidence, I will scale down further or fall back to activation_messaging (memory_91), which is the cheaper adjacent lever. I am explicitly NOT choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 says discount-led acquisition sharply damages retention, which directly contradicts the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue — matching the competitor on price would buy volume that erodes. referral_incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does not address the funnel regression. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is about a different segment than the one bleeding. Downstream value risk is real and flagged: stripping signup fields and onboarding steps removes qualification signal, so it can raise raw activation while lowering lead quality, sales routing accuracy, and eventual qualified revenue — the exact metric I am optimizing. So the test runs guarded: retention, paid-conversion, and qualified-pipeline-per-signup as blocking guardrails, not just completion/activation as success metrics, and any removed field must be recoverable in-product later. Small guarded test rather than broad rollout because the supporting memories are inherited summaries whose provenance I have not yet confirmed, and because the market context (aggressive competitor pricing) differs from the context in which those lifts were originally observed — the prior may simply not transfer.
